title: Polish Film Festival North America
deck: Mid-century Polish illustration meets the Hollywood Sign.
lede: A Polish film festival held in Los Angeles got a poster that belongs to both cities' traditions, painted after rounds of red-marker studies.
challenge: The Polish Film Festival North America is held in Los Angeles. Its identity had to speak to two cultures at once: Polish cinema and its great tradition of poster illustration, and Hollywood, where the films are shown.
work: The answer was a painting. The poster blends mid-century Polish illustration with Hollywood iconography: the red carpet, Walk of Fame stars, the Hollywood Sign and landmarks, rendered in a bold, painterly style. A couple walks across a globe ringed with Hollywood landmarks.

The process ran from concept sketches and rendering studies to digital painting. It began with pencil thumbnails, then red-marker studies of the composition, the iconography (including a map of Poland), the couple, a Polish folk figure and a man in a hat. A six-panel study took the woman's face from sketch to paint. Then came a flat-color block-in with palette swatches, a pass that added palm trees and landmarks, and a final painterly pass with a textured ground.
The symbols are explained in an annotated version of the poster, from the Polish White Eagle crest to the Lee Strasberg Theatre. An alternate Los Angeles edition followed.
credits: Dalton Corr: creative direction, illustration, festival logo
